newsitem.title: JORDAN: Amman stocks lower at end of weekly trade.
newsitem.headline: Amman stocks lower at end of weekly trade.

text.p: Jordanian shares closed slightly lower at end of weekly trade on Wednesday in select demand on firms expected to post healthy half-year earnings, dealers said.

The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index shed 0.13 percent to 166.24 points in moderate 946,957 dinar turnover but demand on a sole cement firm accounted for a third of the day's volume.
"There was demand on stock expected to achieve good profits in the second half of 1997," said Mohammad Abdullah, senior analyst at Pearl Consulting.

Bourse activity has been stagnant over the last few weeks as investors await the coming into law of a cabinet approved recommendation to lift a 50 percent foreign ownership ceiling on most of publicly listed firms.
Jordan Cement Factories rose 0.01 dinars to 4.00 dinars in 351,369 dinars turnover in the day's most heavily traded stock rumoured to have been mainly foreign-inspired.
Aside from El Zay, a leading garments manufacturer which has seen this week a mix of local and foreign interest, there were hardly any substantial deals in a bourse lacking impetus for a rebound.
The textile firm gained 0.06 dinars to 1.57 dinars in 103,588 dinars worth of trade.

The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance, fixed at 100 points at the end of 1994, shed 0.29 percent to 80.89 points, 3.00 percent down since the start of the year. -- Amman newsroom +9626 623776
